title: Navkar Mantra
script:
णमो अरिहंताणं
णमो सिद्धाणं
णमो आयरियाणं
णमो उवज्झायाणं
णमो लोए सव्वसाहूणं
transliteration:
Namo Arihantāṇam
Namo Siddhāṇam
Namo Āyariyāṇam
Namo Uvajjhāyāṇam
Namo Loe Savva-Sāhūṇam
translation:
I bow to the Arihantas (victorious enlightened beings).
I bow to the Siddhas (liberated souls).
I bow to the Āchāryas (spiritual leaders).
I bow to the Upādhyāyas (spiritual teachers).
I bow to all Sādhus (ascetics) in the universe.
These fivefold obeisances destroy all karmas and are the highest auspicious mantra.
tips: Keep all five lines in the same slow, steady rhythm.
Do not rush ‘Savva-Sāhūṇam’ – let the double consonants be clear.

title: Logassa Path (Verses 1–7)
script:
लोगस्स उज्जोअगरे, धम्म तित्थयरे जिणे।
अरिहंते कित्तइस्सं, चउवीसंपि केवली ।।
उसभमजियं च वंदे, संभवमभिणंदणं च सुमई च।
पउमप्पहं सुपासं, जिणं च चंदप्पहं वंदे।।
सुविहिं च पुप्फदंत, सीअल सिज्जंस, वासुपुज्जं च।
विमलमणतं च जिणं, धम्म सतिं च वंदामि।।
कुंथु अरं च मल्लिं, वंदे मुणिसुव्वयं नमिजिणं च।
वंदामि रिट्टनेमि, पासं तह वद्धमाणं च ।।
एवं मए अभिथुआ, विहूयरयमला पहीणजरमरणा।
चउवीसंपि जिणवरा, तित्थयरा मे पसीयंतु।।
कित्तिय वदिय महिया, जे ए लोगस्स उत्तमा सिद्धा।
आरुग्ग बोहिलाभं, समाहिवरमुत्तमं दितु ।।
चंदेसु निम्मलयरा, आइच्चेसु अहियं पयासयरा।
सागरवर गंभीरा, सिद्धा सिद्धिं मम दिसंतु ।।
translation:
In this world I praise the Jinas, establishers of the dharma-tirtha, the twenty-four Kevalīs – Ṛṣabha, Ajita, Saṃbhava, Abhinandana, Sumati, Padmaprabha, Supārśva, Candra-prabha.
I bow to Suvidhi (Suvidhinātha), Puṣpadanta, Śītala, Śreyāṃsa, Vāsupūjya, Vimalanātha, Anantnātha, Dharmanātha, Śāntinātha, Kuṃthanātha, Aranātha, Mallinātha, Munisuvrata, Naminātha, Ariṣṭanemi, Pārśvanātha and Vardhamāna Mahāvīra.
Thus praised by me are those twenty-four Jinas, free from karmic dust, free from old age and death; may those Tīrthaṅkaras be pleased with me.
May the supreme Siddhas of this universe, who are praised by speech, mind and body, grant me health, right understanding, and the highest state of equanimity.
Pure like the moon, brighter than the sun, deep like the ocean – may those Siddhas grant me liberation.
tips: Chant in a flowing Prakrit style; don’t over-Sanskritize sounds like ‘savva’, ‘jiṇaṃ’.
Use light pauses at ‘।’ and ‘।।’ to keep the traditional cadence.
Keep the Tirthankara names very clear, each name getting its own weight.

title: Bhaktamar Stotra – Verses 1–3
script:
भक्तामर प्रणत मौलिमणि प्रभाणा।
मुद्योतकं दलित पाप तमोवितानम् ॥
सम्यक् प्रणम्य जिन पादयुगं युगादा।
वालंबनं भवजले पततां जनानाम् ॥

यः संस्तुतः सकल वाङ्मय तत्वबोधा।
दुद्भूत बुद्धिपटुभिः सुरलोकनाथैः ॥
स्तोत्रैर्जगत्त्रितय चित्तहरैरुदारैः।
स्तोष्ये किलाहमपि तं प्रथमं जिनेन्द्रम् ॥

बुद्ध्या विनाऽपि विबुधार्चित पादपीठं।
स्तोतुं समुद्यत मतिर्विगतत्रपोऽहम् ॥
बालं विहाय जलसंस्थितमिन्दुबिम्बम्।
मन्यः क इच्छति जनः सहसा ग्रहीतुम् ॥
transliteration:
Bhaktāmara praṇata-mauli-maṇi-prabhāṇā,
Mudyotakaṃ dalita-pāpa-tamo-vitānam;
Samyak praṇamya jina-pāda-yugaṃ yugādau,
Vālambanaṃ bhava-jale patatāṃ janānām.

Yaḥ saṃstutaḥ sakala-vāṅmaya-tattva-bodhād,
Udbhūta-buddhi-paṭubhiḥ sura-loka-nāthaiḥ;
Stotraiḥ jagat-tritaya-citta-haraiḥ udāraiḥ,
Stoṣye kilāham api taṃ prathamaṃ Jinendram.

Buddhyā vināpi vibudhārcita-pāda-pīṭhaṃ,
Stotuṃ samudyata-matir vigata-trapo’ham;
Bālaṃ vihāya jala-saṃsthita-mindu-bimbaṃ,
Manyaḥ ka icchati janaḥ sahasā grahītum.
translation:
The radiance of the jewels in the crowns of bowed devotees is reflected in your glory, O Lord, which destroys the vast darkness of sins. At the very beginning of the age, I bow to your pair of lotus feet, the support for beings drowning in the ocean of existence.
You are the First Jinendra, praised by the lords of heaven with noble hymns born of complete scriptural insight, stealing the minds of beings of all three worlds. I too, though small, will sing the praise of that same Supreme Jina.
Though lacking sufficient intellect, I, without shame, set out to praise your feet, worshipped by the wise gods. For apart from a child, who would try to grasp the reflection of the moon in the water?
tips: Use a gentle, devotional Indian chanting tone; let each line breathe.
Sustain long vowels in words like ‘Bhaktāmara’, ‘pāda-yugam’, ‘Jinendram’.
Keep consonant clusters (e.g., ‘tamo-vitānam’, ‘jagat-tritaya’) clear but smooth, without breaking the musical flow.
